# Authentication

The Gorgias API supports two authentication methods:

1. 🔐 Private app → API key
2. 👥 Public app → OAuth2

Using OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps.

For testing purposes, you can perform requests directly from the API Reference using your API keys.

1. Go to any endpoint (e.g: " Retrieve your account")
2. Use your email (username) and your API key

auth.title: Access Tokens (API Keys)
highlights:
Access Tokens (API Keys)

# Access Tokens (API Keys)

> ### 👉
> 
> Please remember that the API key authentication method can be used only for private apps. If you plan to build a public app you have to use OAuth2.

Each access token (or API key) is tied to a specific user and has the same permissions as the user that holds them. Requests made with an access token will act on behalf of a user and will have access to the resources their permissions allow. As an admin, you can easily generate and revoke your access token in the settings of your account.

Example: If you use an Access Token for a user with an Observer Agent role, then you can only do the things that an Observer agent can. Learn more about roles here.

How do I get my API key?

1. Log in to your Gorgias account
2. Navigate to Settings → REST API
3. Click the Create API key button

Once you have your credentials, you can start performing requests directly from the API documentation .

Request example

```
curl --request GET \
  --url https://your-customer-account.gorgias.com/api/account \
  --header 'Authorization: Basic base64encode(USERNAME:API_KEY)'
```

> ### 👉
> 
> Since we're using HTTP Basic Authentication, the `USERNAME:API_KEY` pair has to be a base64 encoded string. Note the `:` between the `USERNAME` and `API_KEY` is a separator used to differentiate between the username and the password.

auth.title: OAuth2 Bearer Token
highlights:
OAuth2 Bearer Token

# OAuth2 Bearer Token

> ### 👉
> 
> Please remember that OAuth2 is required for all public apps to be approved.

OAuth provides a secure way for your application to access Gorgias data without having to store or use sensitive data such as passwords/access tokens of Gorgias users. OAuth2 also provides more granular permissions via OAuth2 Scopes which further increases the security of our customers' data.

In OAuth2, the authentication is done using Bearer Access Tokens. Once you get them you can perform API calls like so:

```
curl --request GET \
  --url https://your-customer-account.gorgias.com/api/account \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR-PLAIN-TEXT-ACCESS-TOKEN'
```

> 📘
> 
> Access Token expiration
> 
> Please remember that OAuth Bearer Access Tokens expire after some time. This is done because sometimes applications only need temporary access to the API (e.g.: one time data import).  If your app needs permanent access you should request the `offline` scope described in OAuth2 Scopes and get a `refresh_token` that can be used to get a new `access_token` when the old one expires.

auth.title: OAuth2 authentication for creating apps with Gorgias
highlights:
OAuth2 authentication for creating apps with Gorgias

# OAuth2 authentication for creating apps with Gorgias

Introduction

In order to be able to have an approved public app with Gorgias, it is required that the app is using OAuth2 for authentication.

You can obtain the OAuth2 token by following these steps and requirements:

1.  Creating an app on the partners’ account
2.  Obtaining the client_id and client_secret
3.  Redirect authorization
4.  Post request to obtain the access token (has a 24 hours expiration time)
5.  Refresh token used to obtain the next token (does not have expiration time)

Partners account and retrieving client_id and client_secret

Once the application is created you will be able to retrieve the client_id and client_secret parameters. *note that the client_id and client_secret are application-bound parameters, and if you are to create more than one application, you would have different parameter values per application.

partners page screenshot for the client_id and client_secret

Authorization redirection

Once the application is approved it will appear on the applications page in the helpdesk, and on that page, the connect app button will be available. The Gorgias users will click on the button to initiate the app installation and they will be redirected to the app URL which was specified on the app submission form in the partners’ account. After you have received that request, the app should send an authorization redirect to the following URL: https://`{subdomain}`.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize

The app authorization is received through redirects. 

Each Gorgias account has its own endpoint, which is defined by the subdomain. On these endpoints are sent all API requests, including the authorization requests.

The parameters which are required to be sent in this redirect are:

-  response_type=code
- client_id=`{your_app_client_id}`
-  redirect_uri=(app’s backend endpoint where to redirect once the app is authorized in order to obtain the tokes)
- scope= scopes

Additional parameters:

-  state=(random string, protecting against CSRF attacks)
-  nonce=(random string, binds it with the token, so we identify the original request that issued it)

You can send multiple scopes in the requests, depending on the requirements of your app.

> 📘
> 
> Example for the redirect URL:
> 
> https://`{subdomain}`.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=6218fa8cfexxxxxxc5929712&state=randomString1234Test&scope=customers%3Aread%20tickets%3Aread%20integrations%3Aread&redirect_uri=`{apps_redirect_uri}`

Authorization page screenshot

Post request to obtain the access token

When the user accepts the authorization for the app, they will be redirected to the redirect_uri that was set in the previous redirect. In this redirect, the code parameter will be sent as well as the state parameter you provided. The code parameter would be required for the POST request in order to obtain the access token.

```
curl -u <client_id>:<client_secret> POST https://`{subdomain}`.gorgias.com/oauth/token
Content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type:authorization_code
redirect_uri:(the same redirect URL you used during the authorization step)
code=`{received_in_redirect}`
```

After this request, you will receive a JSON response containing the access_token as well as the refresh token. Bear in mind that this access token you receive has a 24 hours expiration time.

access_token JSON response example

```
{
"access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6",
"expires_in":86400,
"id_token ... J ... wczov ... Y ... 3J ... 5 ... F1 ... CI ... U ... ZDV ... MjY ... YWNk ... Ei ... NjIw ... 3 ... 5 ... Jle ... 2MjA ... MzM ... F ... ltZSI ... MTYyMDg ... jk ... w ... UiOi ... dFJ ... G ... OWdjZ ... 3 ... zExMSIs ... F ... X2 ... gi ... z ... 3 ... 3 ... z ... nd ... ic ... SI ... wi ... ta ... 5 ... z ... mlv ... EM ... z ... FIcLdT6LB- ... 1 ... ei2 ... lpO ... ZoyojIglJNKYc ... oPYHk1 ... Ex ... 9 ... KS ... w-dsQVumqNXP7 ... 9 ... IOhyJHA37 ... Rq ... Gi ... z ... 4QknZ- ... rgMF ... DF ... QRqrXi ... LOGmESOMJNUd5xKiaQ3 ... t7tWdu ... 7 ... 8sx9UwYC ... ZSzE ... ihn0 ... dg ... xQ9u9oc ... KK7bI ... r3 ... YADUVwBkAzB7J59QN0RZxVnEAtDQZFqViEK0gImWaWpDOMQB ... Npkm3VFZCQYY50qJAA9Pb53XRdvkCyC6R06vYiawgkNUjd4g",
"refresh_token":"Bn8nh9P76uDYZb6wADnV93CyuiqaKaaI00mXQpWFWjfbBR06",
"scope":"openid email profile offline write:all",
"token_type":"Bearer"
}
```

Refresh token used to obtain the next token

With the refresh_token parameter you have received in the first POST request to obtain the access_token, you can send another request, to obtain another access_token.

```
Refresh token request

POST https://`{subdomain}`.gorgias.com/oauth/token
Content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type:refresh_token
refresh_token:(refresh token you received in the response for obtaining the access_token)
```

The JSON response containing the new access token will look like this:

```
{
"access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6IjB6NWZwe",
"expires_in":86400,
"scope":"openid email profile offline write:all",
"token_type":"Bearer"
}
```

> 🚧
> 
> In case the application is deactivated on the helpdesk, in order to obtain the access token again, the entire process for obtaining an access token needs to be repeated.

Testing the OAuth2 flow before application is submitted

In order to test the OAuth2 flow before the application is submitted, you can access it through the partner portal, and on my apps page you can choose the preview option when selecting the additional options of the application, or you can use the following URL to start the installation process: https://`{subdomain}`.gorgias.com/app/settings/integrations/app/`{your_app_client_id}`  You can use your sandbox subdomain and your app client id values in order to generate the testing URL.

Private vs. Public App

# Private vs. Public App

Understand the difference between the two types and decide which one better fits your goals.

Before you start creating your first Gorgias app you need to choose between two types of apps:

🔐 Private apps

These apps should be used if you plan to access only your own Gorgias account data.

- You don't need to follow any special process to create a private app.
- For the authentication method, you can use Access Tokens.

👥 Public apps

These apps are published in our App Store and are available to thousands of shop owners.

- You need to follow a specific process which includes a review from the Gorgias team.

> ### 👉
> 
> Public app authentication can be done only via OAuth2 for which you will need to register on our Developer portal.

auth.title: Access your Gorgias REST API credentials
highlights:
Access your Gorgias REST API credentials

# Access your Gorgias REST API credentials Updated 5 months ago

The Gorgias REST API lets you read and write data in your helpdesk programmatically. To authenticate API requests, Gorgias uses HTTP Basic Authentication with three pieces of information: your base API URL, your email address, and an API key. You can find and manage all three from the REST API settings page in your helpdesk.

Note: API keys are tied to your individual account, not to the helpdesk as a whole.

For full API documentation, visit the Gorgias Developer Documentation.

### Requirements

- Available on all Helpdesk plans
- The account owner and admins can access the API credentials and create API keys

## Find your API credentials

You can find the Base API URL (`https://{your-domain}.gorgias.com/api/`), Username (the email address on your account), and API key in your Gorgias settings. If you don’t have an existing API key, you’ll have to create one first.

1. From your helpdesk, click the  Settings icon in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate Account, then select REST API.
3. Under API Access & Credentials, you'll find the Base API URL, your Username, and Password (API Key).
4. Click Copy next to any field to copy it to your clipboard.

## Create an API key

If you haven't created an API key yet, the Password field will show a Create API key button instead of a key value.

1. From your helpdesk, click the  Settings icon in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate Account, then select REST API.
3. Under Password (API Key), click Create API Key.

Your API key is generated immediately and displayed alongside the other credentials. Your API key grants full access to your account's data. Once you’ve copied it, store it somewhere secure and don’t share it with anyone.

### Reset your API key

You can reset your API key at any time. Resetting generates a new key and immediately invalidates the old one. Any integrations or scripts using the old key will stop working until they're updated with the new one.

1. From your helpdesk, click the  Settings icon in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate Account, then select REST API.
3. Next to the Password (API Key) field, click Reset.
4. Click OK to confirm.

## Import the Postman collection

The REST API settings page also includes a Run in Postman button. Clicking it imports the Gorgias Postman collection with your domain, email address, and API key pre-filled as environment variables, so you can start making requests immediately.

Overview

# Overview

Below are the major steps of the process you need to follow when building a public app with Gorgias.

1. Register on the Developer Portal to submit your app and manage your listing.
2. Create a Draft app in the Developer Portal.
3. Get Gorgias Sandbox to test your app: create a trial account and reach out to [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protect) to convert it into a Sandbox account. 

1. ⚠️ You need to complete steps 1-2 to convert Trial to Sandbox account.
4. Set up OAuth2 for your app.
5. Build your app using our API docs and test it.
6. Complete the rest of the form on the Developer Portal and submit your app for review 

1. ⚠️ Make sure to include testing instructions with a test account
7. Once your app is approved, we will announce it at our next Product Town Hall. 

1. 📢 You can sync with our Partnerships team [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protect) for additional opportunities to promote your app to Gorgias customers.

> 🚀
> 
> Congrats!
> 
> Your app is now available on our App Store and is ready to be used by thousands of Gorgias customers.

gate.title: Building a high-quality Gorgias app
highlights:
# Building a high-quality Gorgias app

We strive to give developers all the tools and features needed to build high-quality app experiences for our shared customers.

To get full access to all Gorgias API features, be listed on the Gorgias App Store, and qualify for exclusive partner benefits, your app needs to use OAuth2 for authentication.

OAuth2 has become the industry standard for creating secure and user-friendly integrations. It's the starting point of building a high-quality app. It also allows us to track app metrics for your app and gives customers more control over their data.

Here are some of the key characteristics of a high-quality Gorgias app:

1. Easy setup: One-click install with OAuth2

Using OAuth2 is mandatory for any 3rd party app. Your app should redirect to the Gorgias OAuth2 page both when the customer initiates the install from inside their Gorgias settings and when they connect the app in your product.

Example flow for install initiated in 3rd party product, using a popup:

A one-click install is what a customer has come to expect of any new app they connect. Please avoid manual installs of HTTP integrations. Your app should add all of its components - sidebar widgets, macros, tags, your webhook subscriptions, etc. - on install.

2. Appropriate OAuth2 scopes

One of the many benefits of using OAuth2 for authentication is that we can give customers better control over who accesses their helpdesk data.

Customers will see which data an app can access, and they can easily revoke permissions by disconnecting the app from their settings.

We expect all partners to wisely choose which scopes they request. If your app is requesting access to data that isn’t needed for your app use case, we will ask you to update the scopes you are accessing.

...

4. Efficient usage of our API

If you're testing your app and notice your app making a lot of unnecessary API calls, get in touch with our API support team. We will look into whether there is a better, more efficient way to accomplish what your apps is trying to do.

Keep our rate limits in mind when building your app, too. Some of our customers receive a ton of data in their accounts. Make sure your app is set up to handle high-volume customer accounts, even during peak times like BFCM.

mcp.title: Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP
highlights:
# Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP Updated 23 days ago

### Who can use this feature?

All Helpdesk plans (AI Agent isn't required)

The Gorgias MCP lets you work with your Gorgias helpdesk using an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT. Once you connect the MCP, your AI assistant can access your Gorgias data and account, so you can manage your helpdesk through conversations. For example, you can use an AI assistant to read and analyze your tickets, audit your account, configure AI Agent, and update your settings.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that lets an AI tool connect to another app like Gorgias.

You can add the Gorgias MCP from Claude's connector directory or ChatGPT's plugin directory. If you use another AI client, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Copilot, you can create a custom connector for the MCP instead. This article covers:

- Requirements
- Who can use the Gorgias MCP?
- Connecting an AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP

- Connecting Claude
- Connecting ChatGPT
- Authorizing your Gorgias account
- Connecting a different AI client, such as Claude Code
- What your AI assistant can do, with prompts to try

## Requirements

- A Gorgias account on any Helpdesk plan.
- An account with Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP-compatible AI assistant.
- Your Gorgias subdomain. This is the `your-brand` part of your account URL (`your-brand.gorgias.com`). You'll enter it when you authorize the connection.

## Who can use the Gorgias MCP?

Everyone can connect the Gorgias MCP, but the actions you can take with your AI assistant depend on the role assigned to your user in Gorgias.

If your company uses Claude Team or Enterprise, or a managed ChatGPT workspace (Business, Enterprise, or Edu), an admin may need to make the Gorgias MCP available before you can connect.

## Connect an AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP

Claude and ChatGPT both list the Gorgias MCP in their connector directories, so you can add it without any manual configuration. Follow the steps for the assistant you use, then authorize your Gorgias account to finish connecting.

### Connect Claude

The Gorgias MCP is available in Claude's connector directory. You can connect the MCP using Claude on the web, desktop app, or mobile app.

On Claude Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner must enable the Gorgias MCP for your organization before members can connect it. Owners can find the steps in Claude's connector documentation. If you don't see the Gorgias MCP in your connectors list, ask your Owner to enable it.

Note: Claude's menus change from time to time. For the most up-to-date steps, refer to Claude's connector documentation.

1. In Claude, select Customize, then select Connectors.
2. Browse the connector directory and search for Gorgias.
3. Select Gorgias MCP, then select Connect. You're redirected to your browser.
4. Authorize your Gorgias account.

### Connect ChatGPT

The Gorgias MCP is available in ChatGPT as a plugin. If you use a managed ChatGPT workspace (Business, Enterprise, or Edu), an admin may need to make the Gorgias MCP available to your workspace first. Admins can find the steps in OpenAI's plugin controls documentation. If you can't find the Gorgias MCP in the directory, ask your workspace admin.

Note: ChatGPT's menus change from time to time. For the most up-to-date steps, refer to OpenAI's plugin documentation.

1. In ChatGPT, open the plugin directory and search for Gorgias MCP.
2. Select Install plugin.
3. Authorize your Gorgias account.

## Authorize your Gorgias account

After you select Connect in Claude or Install plugin in ChatGPT, a browser window opens where you can authorize your AI assistant to connect with the Gorgias MCP.

1. Enter your Gorgias subdomain (example: `your-brand.gorgias.com`), then select Continue.
2. Select Allow Access.
3. Sign in to Gorgias. If you already have an active Gorgias session in your browser, you won't be prompted to sign in.
4. Review the data the Gorgias MCP can access, then select Authorize.
5. Return to Claude or ChatGPT.

That's it. You're connected, and you can start prompting.

## Connect a different AI client

Gorgias MCP works with any MCP-compatible AI client. The setup process varies by client, but the connection URL is the same: https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp

Refer to your AI client's documentation for how to add an HTTP MCP server, then complete the Gorgias authentication step when prompted:

- Claude Code (if you sign in with your Claude account, connectors you add in Claude on the web are also available in Claude Code)
- Codex
- Cursor
- VS Code Copilot

## What your AI assistant can do

Once connected, your AI assistant can read your helpdesk data and take actions on your behalf, within the limits of your Gorgias role. It can work with:

- Tickets: search and read tickets, reply to customers, add internal notes, and update status, priority, and assignee, and add tags.
- Macros and rules: find stale or duplicate macros, create and update macros, and manage automation rules.
- AI Agent: audit your setup, edit tone of voice, guidance, skills, and handover topics, and preview replies before you turn anything on.
- Knowledge: review and draft Help Center articles and AI Agent knowledge.
- Customers and team: look up customer profiles and review your team.
- Insights: pull voice-of-customer trends, response times, ticket volume, and CSAT data.

Some actions can reach your customers or go live, so check the details before you approve them. For example, replying to a ticket or applying a macro can send a message to a customer, and publishing guidance or skills changes how AI Agent responds. By default, Help Center articles and AI Agent guidance are saved as drafts until you publish them, and new rules and actions are created turned off.

You can also explore every tool in the Gorgias MCP, including the Gorgias role each one needs.

...

## FAQ

Can I do anything in Gorgias with my AI assistant?

 

No. Your AI assistant acts as you, so it can only do what your Gorgias role allows. Some actions need a Lead or Admin role. If a request fails with an "Insufficient role" message, review the AI assistants section of user permissions or ask an Admin.

What does my AI assistant see when I connect Gorgias?

 

Your AI assistant receives the ticket, customer, and settings data it retrieves to answer your requests. That data is handled under your AI provider's terms and privacy settings, not Gorgias's. In ChatGPT, plugins can also receive parts of your conversation, such as chat context and memories. Review your provider's data controls before you connect, especially if your company has specific data-handling policies.

What's the difference between the Gorgias MCP and AI Agent?

 

AI Agent helps your shoppers browse, buy, and get support automatically and in your brand's voice. It works inside your helpdesk, across email, chat, SMS, and social media, resolving questions like returns, order changes, and shipping updates and helping new shoppers find products.

The Gorgias MCP is different: it lets you manage your Gorgias account from an external AI tool, like Claude or ChatGPT. AI Agent talks to your shoppers, while the MCP lets you talk to your helpdesk. The two work together. For example, you can use your AI assistant to audit and improve your AI Agent's guidance, skills, and settings.

...

The connection URL shows a page saying "This URL hosts an MCP endpoint" when I open it in a browser.

 

This is expected. The URL is a connection endpoint. It's designed to be added inside your AI client's connectors settings, not opened in a browser tab. When you connect the Gorgias MCP in your AI tool, use this URL as the remote MCP server URL.

Can I connect the Gorgias MCP for multiple brands?

 

Each connection works with one Gorgias account. To connect more than one brand in Claude, add a custom connector for each brand and use that brand's Gorgias subdomain in the connection URL, replacing `YOUR_GORGIAS_SUBDOMAIN`:

`https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp?gorgias_subdomain=YOUR_GORGIAS_SUBDOMAIN`

Authenticate each connection with the Gorgias account that has access to the corresponding brand. For steps on adding a custom connector, refer to Claude's documentation.

mcp.title: Explore Gorgias MCP tools
highlights:
When you ask your AI assistant to do something in Gorgias, it uses tools in the Gorgias MCP. A tool is a single thing the assistant can do, such as listing tickets or creating a macro. Knowing which tools exist, and who can use them, helps you ask for the right thing and understand why a request is refused.

Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP first. Then use this article to see every tool in the Gorgias MCP by area, with the lowest Gorgias role that can use each one. It reflects the Gorgias MCP as of October 2026. This article covers:

- How to read the tables
- Tools that need extra care
- Tools by area

- Tickets
- Customers
- Macros
- Rules
- Tags, custom fields, teams, and SLAs
- Views and view sections
- Widgets
- Account and integrations
- AI Agent settings
- Guidance
- Skills
- Knowledge sources and snippets
- Products
- AI Agent actions
- Opportunities (beta)
- Testing AI Agent
- Help Center
- Audience segments
- Routines
- Reporting and analytics
- Assistant instructions and feedback
- FAQ

## How to read the tables

Each table lists the tool name, what it does, and who can use it.

- Tool: the exact name of the tool. You don't need to type it. Your assistant chooses tools based on your request, and might show you the name when it runs one.
- Type: Read tools look up information and don't change anything. Write tools create, change, or delete something.
- Minimum role: the lowest Gorgias role that can use the tool, based on your role permissions. The role levels build on each other, so a tool available to Lite and above is also available to Basic, Lead, and Admin.

| Minimum role | Who can use the tool |
| --- | --- |
| All roles | Observer, Lite, Basic, Lead, and Admin |
| Lite and above | Lite, Basic, Lead, and Admin |
| Lead and above | Lead and Admin |
| Admin | Admin only |

Your assistant uses your own Gorgias login, so it can use a tool only if your role allows it.

Safe by default. Some tools are cautious unless you tell the assistant otherwise:

- New rules and AI Agent actions, and copies of actions, are created turned off.
- Changes to guidance, skills, and Help Center articles are saved as drafts until you publish them. The exception is when you ask the assistant to publish a new Help Center article right away.
- Macros are archived, not deleted.
- Tools that test AI Agent simulate its actions, except the three marked Changes real data.

## Tools that need extra care

Some tools can reach your customers, change what your customers or AI Agent see right away, or remove something. Each of these tools has a label in the tables below. Review what your assistant is about to do before you approve it.

| Label | What it means | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sends to customers | Can deliver a message to a customer, or let AI Agent respond to customers. | `create_ticket` (only if you ask it to send), `create_message`, `reply_and_close`, `apply_macro`, `enable_ai_agent_on_channel`. |
| Sends to Gorgias | Sends information to Gorgias instead of changing your helpdesk. | `submit_feature_request`. |
| Goes live | Changes something your customers, your team, or AI Agent use right away. | `update_rule` (if the rule is on), `enable_rule`, `update_tone_of_voice`, `update_excluded_handover_topics`, `enable_ai_agent_on_channel`, `publish_guidance`, `publish_skill`, `set_snippet_status`, `set_product_custom_info`, `pin_metafield_definition`, `update_support_action` (if the action is on), `enable_support_action`, `create_help_center_article` (if you ask it to publish), `publish_help_center_article`, `update_help_center_theme`, `update_help_center_extra_html`, `create_routine`, `update_routine` (if the routine is on), `set_routine_enabled`, `trigger_routine`. |
| Changes real data | Runs AI Agent actions against your live store and connected apps, even though it's a test. | `preview_ai_agent_with_live_actions`, `continue_ai_agent_preview_with_live_actions`, `compare_ai_agent_previews_with_live_actions`. |
| Can't be undone | Permanently removes or converts something. No tool in the Gorgias MCP can reverse it. | `discard_draft_guidance`, `delete_support_action`, `convert_to_advanced_view`, `discard_help_center_article_draft`. |
| Deletes | Deletes an item. The Gorgias MCP has no tool to restore it. | `delete_view`, `delete_view_section`, `delete_widget`, `delete_routine`. |

...

### Tickets

| Tool | What it does | Type | Minimum role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_tickets` | List tickets, newest first by default. To filter by status, channel, or assignee, pass a view you've already created. | Read | All roles |
| `search_tickets` | Search ticket subjects, messages, and customer details for a word or phrase. | Read | All roles |
| `get_ticket` | Get one ticket with its tags, summary, and, if you ask for them, its messages. | Read | All roles |
| `list_ticket_audit_events` | List the history of changes on one ticket, such as status and assignee changes. | Read | All roles |
| `create_ticket` | Open a new ticket with a first message. By default, it logs a message from the customer and sends nothing. Sends to customers (only if you ask it to send). | Write | Lite and above |
| `create_message` | Post a message on a ticket. A reply can be delivered to the customer, and it can also be sent to another address. Sends to customers. | Write | Lite and above |
| `reply_and_close` | Send a reply to the customer and close the ticket in one step. Sends to customers. | Write | Lite and above |
| `add_internal_note` | Add an internal note to a ticket. Customers can't see it. | Write | All roles |
| `update_tickets` | Update the status, priority, or assignee of one or many tickets, and add tags to them. It adds tags and doesn't remove them. | Write | Lite and above |
| `snooze_ticket` | Snooze a ticket until a date and time you choose, with an optional note. | Write | Lite and above |
| `escalate_ticket` | Assign a ticket to a team, add the escalated tag, and leave a note explaining why. | Write | Lite and above |
| `update_ticket_custom_fields` | Replace the values of a ticket's custom fields. | Write | Lite and above |
| `get_job` | Check the progress of a background job, such as one started by `update_tickets` or `apply_macro`. | Read | All roles |

...

Check your Claude or ChatGPT settings for tool permissions, and review each request before you approve it.

mcp.title: Official Information About Gorgias
highlights:
### Gorgias in AI assistants

The Gorgias MCP lets brands work with their Gorgias account through an AI assistant. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that lets an AI tool connect to another app. Once connected, the assistant can read and analyze tickets, reply to customers, manage macros and rules, audit and configure AI Agent, draft Help Center articles, and pull insights like ticket volume, response times, and CSAT. What it can do depends on the user's role in Gorgias. Changes that reach customers or go live are reviewed first: Help Center articles and AI Agent guidance are saved as drafts, and new rules start turned off.

The Gorgias MCP is included on every Helpdesk plan. AI Agent is not required.

- Claude: add Gorgias MCP from Claude's connector directory (web, desktop, or mobile).

- ChatGPT: install Gorgias MCP from ChatGPT's plugin directory.

- Other AI clients, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and VS Code Copilot: add https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp as an HTTP MCP server. If you open this URL in a browser, you'll see a page saying it hosts an MCP endpoint. That's expected.

To finish connecting, enter your Gorgias subdomain (your-brand.gorgias.com), sign in to Gorgias, and authorize access. On Claude Team or Enterprise, or a managed ChatGPT workspace, an admin may need to enable the Gorgias MCP first.

Setup guide: https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/connect-your-ai-assistant-to-the-gorgias-mcp-6310546
